title: Around the Basketball Court
description: Explore basketball through familiar court features, equipment, and the actions seen during play.
cardDescription: Explore basketball through familiar court features, equipment, and the actions seen during play.
focus: The clues identify visible objects and common playing terms. They do not depend on remembering a player or a season.
solvingTip: Look for a court feature, a player role, or an action with the ball.
words: Team game played by shooting a ball through a raised hoop
Circular target through which a basketball is shot
Metal ring supporting a basketball net
Hanging mesh attached beneath a basketball rim
Flat panel behind a basketball hoop
To bounce the ball repeatedly while moving in basketball
To send the ball to a teammate
Attempt to send a basketball through the hoop
Ball recovered after a missed basketball shot
Basketball position often associated with ball handling
Basketball position traditionally associated with play near the basket
Rule violation involving illegal contact in basketball
Successful basketball shot through the hoop

answerNotes.DRIBBLE: Dribbling uses repeated bounces. It differs from passing the ball to a teammate.
answerNotes.REBOUND: A rebound follows a missed shot. It can refer to the recovered ball or the act of gaining it.
answerNotes.CENTER: Center names a playing position here. It is not merely the middle location of the court.
answerNotes.BACKBOARD: The backboard is the panel behind the rim. It is separate from the circular hoop itself.

title: An American Football Afternoon
description: Follow an American football game through familiar actions, field terms, and equipment.
cardDescription: Follow an American football game through familiar actions, field terms, and equipment.
focus: The clues use the American game meaning of football. Short action words help identify the sport without requiring a rule-book calculation.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue names a field area, an action, or a stage of play.
words: American team game played with an oval ball and end zones
To stop a ball carrier by bringing the player down legally
To throw the football toward an eligible teammate
To carry a football while moving on foot
Kick made from the hands before the dropped ball touches the ground
To strike the football with the foot
Target formed by uprights and a crossbar in football
One play in a team’s series of football opportunities
Length unit used to mark an American football field
Scoring area beyond a football goal line
Protective headgear worn by an American football player
Players acting together on one football side
Close gathering of players to discuss the next play
Action that transfers the ball to begin a football play

answerNotes.DOWN: Down names one play in this football setting. It does not describe a direction of movement.
answerNotes.ENDZONE: End zone is normally written as two words. The crossword joins its letters into one grid entry.
answerNotes.HUDDLE: A huddle is a brief close gathering. It names the group arrangement rather than one particular player.
answerNotes.SNAP: A snap starts the play by transferring the ball. The clue uses a sporting action rather than a clothing fastener.

title: At the Hockey Rink
description: Step beside the ice with familiar words for hockey equipment, playing space, and simple actions.
cardDescription: Step beside the ice with familiar words for hockey equipment, playing space, and simple actions.
focus: The clues identify the objects and units seen during an ice-hockey game. Shape and purpose distinguish the equipment.
solvingTip: Look for a playing object, a protective item, or a term used during the action.
words: Ice game in which players use sticks to move a puck
Flat hard disk struck in ice hockey
Long implement used to direct a hockey puck
Boot with a blade used to glide on ice
Frozen playing surface in an indoor hockey rink
Enclosed area used for skating or ice hockey
Scoring target defended by a hockey goalie
Mesh forming the back of a hockey goal
Protective face covering used by a hockey goalie
Protective cushion worn by a hockey player
Protective hand covering worn while holding a hockey stick
One of the main time divisions in a hockey game
To direct the puck to a teammate
Attempt to send the puck into the goal

answerNotes.PUCK: A puck is a flat disk. Its shape distinguishes hockey’s playing object from the balls used in many sports.
answerNotes.RINK: A rink is the playing or skating area. It is not a particular skate or piece of protective gear.
answerNotes.PERIOD: Period names a division of playing time. The word does not mean a punctuation mark here.
answerNotes.SKATE: A skate is the complete boot-and-blade item. The blade is one part of that equipment.

title: Soccer on the Local Field
description: Read familiar soccer words for equipment, positions, and the ways a ball moves around the field.
cardDescription: Read familiar soccer words for equipment, positions, and the ways a ball moves around the field.
focus: The clues describe soccer rather than American football. Some answers are ordinary words with a specific sporting meaning.
solvingTip: Check whether a clue asks for a place, a player, or an action with the ball.
words: Game in which teams primarily kick a ball toward goals
Round object kicked during a soccer match
Target opening into which a soccer team tries to score
Mesh attached to the back of a soccer goal
Outdoor playing area for a soccer match
Another word for a soccer playing field
To send a soccer ball to a teammate
To strike the soccer ball with the foot
Play in which the ball is struck with the head

Action used to return a ball from the sideline in soccer
Illegal action called by a soccer referee
Match result in which neither soccer team wins

answerNotes.PITCH: Pitch names the field in this soccer clue. It has a different sporting meaning in baseball.
answerNotes.HEADER: A header uses the head to play the ball. The clue asks for the play name rather than a written heading.
answerNotes.KEEPER: Keeper is a short form of goalkeeper. The clue identifies the role rather than a particular player.
answerNotes.DRAW: A draw is a level result. It is not the act of taking a card or making a picture in this context.

title: Across the Volleyball Net
description: Explore volleyball through familiar ball actions, court words, and short descriptions of a rally.
cardDescription: Explore volleyball through familiar ball actions, court words, and short descriptions of a rally.
focus: These definitions identify common volleyball terms without requiring detailed scoring knowledge. Several words have everyday meanings outside sport.
solvingTip: Look for an action near the net, a ball-handling move, or a unit of play.
words: Team game played by sending a ball over a high net
Inflated playing object used in volleyball
Raised mesh barrier separating volleyball teams
Hit that begins a volleyball rally
Forceful downward attack hit in volleyball
Controlled overhead pass preparing an attack
Defensive play lifting a low attacked ball
Action near the net intended to stop an opponent’s attack
To change court positions in an ordered pattern
Group playing on one side of a volleyball net
One unit added to a volleyball score
Sequence of play beginning with a serve
Informal term for a forearm pass

answerNotes.SET: Set names a ball-handling move here. It does not mean a collection of equipment or a tennis scoring division.
answerNotes.DIG: A dig is a defensive recovery of an attacked ball. The word is used for sport rather than moving soil.
answerNotes.SPIKE: A spike is a strong attacking hit. It differs from the controlled preparation called a set.
answerNotes.RALLY: A rally is a connected sequence of play. It begins with a serve and ends when play stops for a decision.
